meta.title: Swahili Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 284 phrases · both directions, as two cards per phrase
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Swahili → English (see the phrase, recall the meaning) and English → Swahili (see an English meaning, recall the Swahili). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule. 284 phrases and expressions, built on the five Swahili level decks (A1 to C1): every phrase Wiktionary lists for Swahili that those decks do not already teach, less a few left out as crude, sexual, an insult or rare — 35 set phrases and greetings, 29 proverbs (methali), 34 idioms, and 186 other multi-word expressions, most of them a verb with its noun (piga simu, to phone; fanya kazi, to work) or a phrase that works as one adverb or preposition (kwa kweli, really; kwa niaba ya, on behalf of). Compound nouns and spelled-out numbers are words, not phrases, and are left to the level decks. The cards are dealt by how often each phrase occurs in film and television subtitles and the Global Voices news site together — a verb phrase counted with its verb conjugated (alipiga simu, she phoned) — so the everyday ones come first; the phrases those never use, most of the proverbs among them, are kept and dealt last rather than left out. Real example sentences come with 62 of the 284, three apiece for 22 of them; Tatoeba's Swahili is small, and a proverb is seldom in it. Sources. Phrases, meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: counted from OpenSubtitles 2024 and Global Voices (CC BY 3.0), both as distributed by OPUS. Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
